problems.prompt: A concept's mastery estimate is 0.99 after a long streak of correct answers. You answer the next question wrong. What is the most likely effect?

choices.text: It drops back near 0.5, as if you were starting over
It stays exactly flat — a single answer never moves the estimate
It dips a little, staying above the 0.85 learned threshold

problems.solution: At 0.99 the model is nearly sure you know the concept, and it expects someone who knows it to slip about one time in ten, so one miss is weak evidence: the estimate falls to about 0.93, still above 0.85. From 0.9 the same miss would land near 0.53 — the size of the move depends on where the estimate sits.

problems.prompt: Two concepts both sit at mastery 0.6. One has ten prior answers behind that number; the other has one. You get the next question wrong on both. Which estimate drops further?

choices.text: The one with only one prior answer — with little history the estimate is more sensitive
The one with ten prior answers — more history means more room for it to fall
They drop by the same amount — the update uses only the current estimate and this answer
Neither drops — the estimate only moves on correct answers

problems.solution: The update reads two things: the current estimate and whether this answer was right. Ten answers or one, both histories are already folded into the 0.6, so the same miss takes both to the same place (about 0.16).
